words.meaning: A network guard that lets data in or out based on a list of rules.
A box that links the computers and devices in one office network.
To move work from the main system to its standby copy.
A spare copy of a system, kept ready to take over.
Left with no owner and not attached to anything that uses it.
A saved copy of a disk at one moment in time.
A private, locked link between two networks over the internet.
A private, locked connection to the work network over the internet.
A numbered door on a computer. Each kind of network connection uses its own port.
The internet's address book. It turns names like example.com into number addresses.
Time to live. How long other computers keep a saved web address before checking again.
The main chip that does a computer's work. CPU use shows how busy it is.
The built-in software that runs a device, like a switch or router.
Short for configuration. The saved settings that tell a device how to work.
A formal check of a company's records. An auditor is the person who does it.
A separate network that runs on the same switch and cables as others.
The set of network addresses handed out to devices as they join.
A digital ID for a website. It proves the site's name and keeps visits private.
Cheap, slow storage for data that is rarely opened.
Remote desktop protocol. A way to see and control a computer from far away.
A written request for a planned change, with its steps, time and approval.
The steps to undo a change and go back to how things were.
The rule for how long data must be kept before it can be deleted.
Labels on cloud items that say who owns them and what they are for.
Extra power to install apps, change settings and manage other accounts.
